additional_concerns: Retention of accountability, supervisory conduct and operational outcomes are distinct. The source supplies no complete fulfillment test: neither formal allocation alone nor supervision alone establishes effective retention, and an operational failure alone does not establish loss of accountability.

The ownership-record and operational-compatibility duty is separate from retention. The two supplied 6.8 excerpts concern maintaining a register; the fuller excerpt also requires disclosure of its location on request. Neither supplies a general test of retained provider accountability.

The valuation supervision provision applies to third-party valuation. The intermediary provisions have their own issuance, dealing, advice or portfolio-management conditions. Importing them as universal Product Provider fulfillment criteria would require an applicability argument.

Paragraph 14 grammatically attaches the request condition to demonstration, leaving confirmation unconditioned. Footnote 5 can be read as specifying the content of that demonstration or as requiring demonstration independently. No request therefore does not establish that all assurance duties are inactive.

Footnote 5 specifies minimum compliance with paragraphs 10–13 and high confidence concerning smart-contract vulnerabilities and security flaws. The supplied extracts do not establish the complete contents of paragraphs 10–13. Paragraphs 15 and 16 separately condition third-party audit or verification and a satisfactory legal opinion on an SFC request; neither is automatically required to prove retention.

The referenced Appendix factors are not supplied, and no external dependency IDs are available. Their applicable contents, any governing fulfillment standard and actual governance evidence remain necessary for a broader fulfillment assessment. No executable restrictions or permissions can be inspected because no formalization is supplied.

question_relation.rationale: The exact question assesses retained accountability, not fulfillment of SFC demonstration duties or overall compliance. Demonstration may furnish evidence about retention, but its request trigger and satisfaction standard are not conditions of retaining responsibility.

source_support.rationale: Paragraph 14 expressly supports demonstration upon request to the SFC's satisfaction of all listed matters. Footnote 5 adds minimum content and a high-confidence qualification. Its omission of the request condition leaves rival readings about demonstration without a request, but does not negate the stated upon-request duty. The claim is supported without reading 'upon request' as 'only upon request'.
